questions.question_text:
A train's speed-time graph rises in a straight line from $0$ to $18$ m/s in $100$ seconds, remains at $18$ m/s until $400$ seconds, then falls in a straight line to zero at $500$ seconds.
Find the total distance travelled, in m.

options.why: used full rectangles for the accelerating and decelerating stages, giving $18\times500=9000$ m
included only the cruising rectangle, giving $18\times(400-100)=5400$ m
included only the accelerating and decelerating triangles, giving $900+900=1800$ m, and omitted cruising

questions.solution_text:
The cruising stage lasts $400-100=300$ seconds, and the decelerating stage lasts $500-400=100$ seconds.
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}\times100\times18+18\times300+\dfrac{1}{2}\times100\times18$
$=900+5400+900$
$=7200\text{ m}$
